Owner verified on 5.2.37 and 5.3.9, and it was re-verified here: bash exits only for the command following the FINAL && or ||, so a failing LEFT operand — the debug-log idiom `[[ "${VERBOSE_KKLASS:-}" == "debug" ]] && echo ... >&2` that sits on every error path — does not abort; the documented `return 1` is reached. deviations: D3 is implemented with `static proc` + a unit-local `tpath._ret`, NOT `static func` + kk._return. kklass's THIN static dispatcher (a class without static variables) re-prints kk._return's value unconditionally — on a direct call too — so `static func` would echo on every call, which is the opposite of what D3 asks for. The semantics D3 specifies (direct = RESULT, no fork; $( ) prints once) are met exactly, and no kklass change was needed. The idiom is written into kcl/README.md 1.1 so P5/P6/P7 do not rediscover it.

G6-05 does NOT use `cygpath -w` + `cmd mklink`: measured on this box, mklink answers 'insufficient privileges' even with correct Windows paths, while `MSYS=winsymlinks:native ln -s` creates a real link. The G6 report states the opposite; both were run.

The three listings gained an optional FOURTH argument, the name of a caller array (kcl/README 1.7). Without it a file name containing a newline is indistinguishable from two names. The old newline-joined RESULT is unchanged, so no existing call breaks.
`tfile.readAllTextVar FILE NAME` puts the output-variable name LAST, matching the `str.split "$s" ',' parts` shape of kcl/README 1.7 (R13 does not fix the order).
tdirectory's `Error: ...` messages moved behind VERBOSE_KKLASS=debug (kcl/README 1.2). Not a G6 finding, but the unit printed on every miss and the contract says otherwise.

TDIRECTORY_COLLATE and the `local LC_ALL=` / `LC_COLLATE=en_US.UTF-8` override inside the listings are gone: the order is the ambient locale's (the runners pin C.UTF-8 = codepoint order). tdirectory 013/014 expectations were rewritten from en_US order to codepoint order.
The read-only attribute is derived from the stat MODE, not from `[[ ! -w ]]`: `-w` follows a symlink unconditionally, which is why both FollowLink answers were identical (the mechanism of G6-14).

Access-time VALUES are not asserted after an intervening access: NTFS rewrites a stored access time that is far in the past on the next access (measured). The setters are asserted with an immediate `stat -c %X`, and the getter formatting is proven on the write time, which is stable. tdirectory 022/024 ('two reads must be identical') were rewritten to 'both well formed and within 2 s' for the same reason.

P4.title: tcustomapplication: faithful FPC 3.2.2 custapp port (D4) — CheckOptions/FindOptionIndex/GetOptionAtIndex/GetOptionValue(s)/HasOption/GetNonOptions, ParamCount/Params, DoRun+Run, tests rewritten
P4.upstream_reference: FPC 3.2.2 packages/fcl-base/src/custapp.pp, fetched from https://gitlab.com/freepascal.org/fpc/source/-/raw/release_3_2_2/packages/fcl-base/src/custapp.pp (784 lines) — there is no local FPC installation on this machine. The whole option parser was ported from that file line by line, not from memory.

TCA-01.fix: `--name=value` is the only long-option value syntax, exactly as FPC. FindOptionIndex cuts the option NAME at the first '=' (`P:=Pos('=',O); If (P<>0) then O:=Copy(O,1,P-1)`), and GetOptionAtIndex returns everything after that '=' — no '=' means NO value, so `--out file` answers '' and `file` stays a non-option. The old build compared the whole token, so the option was literally named `config=data.ini` and the tests had adopted `verbose=true` as an option name.

TCA-02.fix: `:` and `::` in ShortOptions and in a long option name are honoured: a required argument missing gives SErrOptionNeeded, an argument on a switch gives SErrNoOptionAllowed, `::` is silent either way, and a short option's value is CONSUMED (`Inc(I)` skips it) so it is not counted as a non-option. The cluster rule is FPC's: a value-taking short option must be last in its argument (`-cv x` with spec `c:v` errors, `-vc x` does not).

TCA-03.fix: ParamCount and Params read the STORED argv, not the method call's own `$#`/`${!i}`. Indices are FPC's ParamStr indices: Params[0] = ExeName = $0, Params[1..ParamCount] = the arguments, anything else ''. The index goes through kk.isInt first (D1).
TCA-03.red_before: 011: 4 FAIL / 4 PASS (every old assertion was guarded by `if ParamCount>0`, which was never true); 008: 5 FAIL

TCA-04.fix: the `"$@"` forwarding into _EnsureArgsInitialized is gone together with _EnsureArgsInitialized and _PrepareArguments. A fresh instance has ParamCount 0; an application is given its command line by `TCustomApplication.new app "$@"` or `app.SetArgs "$@"` and nothing else. Before, `a.GetNonOptions "" "" nn` on a fresh app answered 3 — the method's own three parameters.
TCA-04.test: tests/019_CommandLineArgsRealParameters.sh (rewritten: helper scripts in the suite temp dir, not /tmp, and the unit found relative to the test file, not by guessing the repository path), 017

TCA-06.fix: CaseSensitiveOptions is consulted on every path, with FPC's exact asymmetry: FindOptionIndex and FindLongOpt UpperCase both sides, CheckOptions LowerCases the short-option spec and the argument. It was stored and never read.
TCA-06.test: tests/022_CaseSensitiveOptions.sh (four new blocks — the file never set the property to false before), 005

TCA-07.fix: GetOptionValues SHORT LONG [ARRAY] fills a caller array and returns the COUNT in RESULT (R10, kcl README 1.7); the name is validated and a reserved/malformed one is rc 2. The old `"count:${values[*]}"` string joined on IFS, so `-f 'a b' -f c` was indistinguishable from three values and a caller with IFS=: got a different answer.

TCA-08.fix: whether LongOpts is an array or a separated string is decided by that argument ALONE — a valid identifier naming an existing array variable (checked with `declare -p` plus `${ref@a}`, both builtins) is the array, everything else is FPC's String overload split on space/tab/CR/LF. It used to depend on whether Opts/NonOpts had been passed, and `("${long_ref[@]:-}")` turned an empty array into one empty option name.

TCA-09.fix: AllErrors is honoured: the loop condition is FPC's `While (I<=ParamCount) and ((Result='') or AllErrors)`, and AddToResult joins the messages with a newline (sLineBreak).

TCA-10.fix: `proc DoRun` added and `Run` is FPC's `Repeat Try DoRun except HandleException(Self) Until Terminated` — an in-process loop reading the Terminated property nameref, with no `$( )` and no `sleep`. A non-zero status from DoRun is what HandleException is given (bash has no exceptions). The base DoRun terminates, so the base class is usable; FPC's is empty, which would spin forever.
TCA-10.test: tests/004_RunOperations.sh (rewritten in full, with two descendant classes overriding DoRun), 016, 031
TCA-10.red_before: 004: the old busy loop never returned — the file TIMED OUT at 90 s (rc 124) with 1 FAIL / 0 PASS; 016 and 031 timed out the same way

TCA-11.fix: Location is ExtractFilePath(ParamStr(0)) computed from `$0`, in bash, with no fork. BASH_SOURCE[0] inside an eval'd kklass method body is kklass.sh, which is why the old member answered with the framework's directory.
TCA-11.test: tests/008_PropertiesAndIntegration.sh (two blocks, one of them a probe script in another directory)

TCA-12.fix: Terminate sets a plain global EXITCODE with `declare -g`, never `export`. FPC assigns the program variable ExitCode, which is not in the environment either.

TCA-13.fix: a lone `-` is `Invalid option at position N: "-"` (FPC's `Length(O)<2` branch) and a mid-argv `--` is a long option with an empty name, `Invalid option at position N: ""`. SetArgs no longer swallows a leading `--`: it stores its arguments verbatim, so an application can actually receive one.

TCA-15.fix: GetEnvironmentList reads `compgen -e` (a builtin) instead of `env | sort`, and takes each value with `${!name}`, so a value containing a newline stays ONE entry instead of becoming several bogus ones. FPC does not sort either. It is now a func returning the entry count and validating the output-array name.
TCA-15.test: tests/007_EnvironmentAndLogging.sh (five blocks, one of them shadowing env(1) and sort(1) with canaries that leave a file)

TCA-16.fix: Log formats with `printf -v` (its arguments were dropped), filters by EXACT membership in the space/comma separated EventLogFilter (it was a substring match, so `etErr` passed a filter of `etError`), and writes to stderr instead of stdout. A bad format is reported as FPC does: `Error formatting message "%s" with %d arguments`, logged as etError.
TCA-16.red_before: 010: 1 FAIL (the substring case); 014: 6 FAIL / 0 PASS; part of the 11 FAIL in 007

TCA-17.fix: R10 confirmed against the source: FPC's FindOptionIndex starts at ParamCount and decrements, so the LAST occurrence wins, and StartAt is the highest index to consider (StartAt 0 finds nothing). GetOptionValues collects every short match and then every long match by the same downward walk, which is why its values come back last-first.
TCA-17.red_before: 005: the block failed on the old first-occurrence scan; 018 TIMED OUT (rc 124) because the old StartAt semantics never terminated the walk

TCA-18.fix: the three FPC ResourceStrings verbatim, with the 1-based position: `Invalid option at position %d: "%s"`, `Option at position %d does not allow an argument: %s`, `Option at position %d needs an argument : %s` (the space before the colon is FPC's).

TCA-19.fix: dead code removed: the `unset -f tcustomapplication._call_silent` line, the _CachedShortOpts / _CachedGetoptOpts / _ArgsInitialized / _OptionCharCache / _DoubleOptionCharCache state entries, and the members _EnsureArgsInitialized / _PrepareArguments / _GetNextArgValue / _ValidateOption / _ParseLongOpts.

TCA-20.fix: HandleException runs OnException only when `declare -F` says it names a defined function; anything else falls back to ShowException, with a diagnostic under VERBOSE_KKLASS=debug. `OnException = "my handler"` used to reach the shell as a command.

gate.bench: the unit has no bench.sh. The fork claim is pinned structurally instead: 031_Contract.sh asserts that the eight parser helpers (tca._findIndex, _optionAt, _checkOptions, _findLongOpt, _longOpts, _addErr, _isName, _outName) contain no command substitution and no backquote at all (declare -f, with `$((` removed first), that BASHPID is unchanged across CheckOptions + GetOptionValue and RESULT reaches the caller, and 004 records BASHPID inside every DoRun pass of Run.

deviations: The option parser is EIGHT PLAIN SHELL FUNCTIONS (`tca._*`), not kklass members. They take the instance's data array by name, so they cost no dispatch, cannot print into a caller's `$( )` (which is what kk.call_silent existed to prevent), and are directly testable. The public members stay thin. Their answers travel in four module-private globals (__TCA_IDX, __TCA_LONG, __TCA_VAL, __TCA_ERR) rather than in RESULT, which belongs to the member that called them.

FindOptionIndex takes a (short, long) PAIR. FPC's takes one name plus a `var LongOpt` out-parameter and its callers try the short name, then the long one; the port carries the pair through the whole option API, so the composition is inside the member. An EMPTY name means 'not given' and is not searched — FPC passes the impossible character #255 for exactly that purpose in GetOptionValue(S).
GetOptionAtIndex is PUBLIC (protected in FPC): the (short, long) merge above hides which of the two forms matched, so a caller that wants the value at a known index needs the member.

GetNonOptions answers rc 1 + RESULT='' where FPC raises EListError, and leaves the output array untouched (D2). Note the consequence for callers: a command line with a lone `-`, a mid-argv `--` or an unknown option now FAILS instead of counting those as non-options.

GetOptionValues returns its values in FPC's order, which is REVERSE command-line order (the downward scan of TCA-17/R10). Faithful, and surprising enough that both the README and the tests say so; overrule it and the change is two loops.

FPC's CheckOptions reads PAST THE END of a short-option cluster. `O:=O[j]` truncates O to one character while the loop keeps indexing `O[j]` against the ORIGINAL length; `-cv` with the spec `c::v` reaches it without any error being raised. The port keeps the scan string intact and records the consuming option in a separate variable, which is identical to FPC for every input where FPC stays in bounds. This is the one place where the port deliberately does not reproduce upstream.
Location returns the directory WITHOUT a trailing separator (FPC's ExtractFilePath keeps one) and '.' when $0 has no directory part, matching tpath.getDirectoryName and the rest of kcl.
Log writes to stderr. FPC's DoLog is empty and descendants override it; a bash port has to do something, and a log line is a diagnostic, not the program's output.
Run maps a non-zero status from DoRun onto FPC's `except HandleException(Self)`, and the base DoRun TERMINATES (FPC's is empty, which would make the inherited Run spin forever).

The constructor defaults StopOnException=true, ExceptionExitCode=1 and Title='Application'; FPC leaves them False, 0 and ''. These are the port's existing values and are kept deliberately (an unhandled error should stop a script), listed under 'Differences from FPC' in the unit README. No finding asked for them.

GetEnvironmentList uses one process substitution per call (`readarray -t < <(compgen -e)`) because bash cannot enumerate exported names without one. That is one fork per CALL, not per element, and it replaces two forks plus a pipe.

The unit gained the LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 self-heal block from kcl/README.md 1.6: it was not there, and CaseSensitiveOptions=false folds case with ${s,,}/${s^^}, which corrupts UTF-8 in the C locale on 5.2 (D6).
`echo` -> `printf` in ShowException and Log. The unit was not one of the six 'printing' units P1 swept, so two echo call sites had survived (X-ECHO).
The FPC report's note that GetOptionAtIndex hard-codes '-' (repro A15) is WRONG: custapp.pp:397 compares with the OptionChar property. The port does the same, and 023 pins it.
